name: Pakka Ltd
about: Incorporated in 1981, Yash Pakka Limited, is engaged in the business of specialty packaging products manufacturing and trading in specialty papers and Moulded (Tableware) products. [1]

flags.text: Debtor days rose from 22 to 47 in three years: customers are taking longer to pay
Cash conversion cycle stretched from 357 to 408 days in three years
Debt/equity up from 0.73 to 1.04 in three years
Capital work-in-progress is 362% of fixed assets: a big build-out is still to be commissioned
Share capital up 23% in three years: new shares from an issue, a merger or a bonus. Only the first two dilute
Free cash flow negative in 3 of the last 5 years

business.what: Pakka Limited manufactures flexible packaging, wrap and carry products, and food service disposables. It utilizes sugarcane bagasse-based pulp and is expanding into high-quality flexible packaging substrates through its new PM4 machine project.

segments.name: Wrap & Carry
segments.comment: Revenue grew 43% year-on-year; operational performance improved despite higher financing costs.

segments.name: Food Services
segments.comment: Revenue grew 34% year-on-year; division recorded a loss due to structural manufacturing changes.

ledger.promise: Commission Project Jagruti by end of CY 2025
ledger.quote: the idea is we are definitely planning to Commission Jagriti within this calendar year.
ledger.actual: Target pushed to end FY26 in Q1 FY26, 1st August 2026 in Q3 FY26, and Q3 FY27 in Q1 FY27 call.

ledger.promise: Commission PM3 production by June or July 2025
ledger.quote: There are a few delays in supply, not at our end, so it's going to be June, July.
ledger.actual: No subsequent call or filing provided confirmation or status updates on PM3 production start.

ledger.promise: Start PM4 machine in 6 to 8 months (Feb–Apr 2026)
ledger.quote: We are working on setting up PM4 which will be started in the next 6 to 8 months
ledger.actual: Timeline pushed to end of October or November 2026 in the Q1 FY27 call.

ledger.promise: Commission Guatemala project stage 1 by June 2026
ledger.quote: our aim is to have the project live by June 2026.
ledger.actual: Project postponed by 3-4 quarters and put in abeyance as per Q3 FY26 call.

ledger.promise: Maintain peak debt level at around ₹600 crore
ledger.quote: I would say if you take both, it'll be about 600 crores as the peak debt level
ledger.actual: Reported borrowings stood at ₹460 crore in FY26 and ₹542 crore in FY27.

ledger.promise: Deliver FY27 EBITDA margin of 18% or 19%
ledger.quote: definitely there is no doubt that the EBITDA margin should be about 18 or 19% on the total on the total sales which comes for FY27.
ledger.actual: Q1 FY27 margin was 13.1% and Q2 FY27 was 14.1%, resulting in H1 FY27 margin of 13.3%.

ledger.promise: Achieve consolidated revenue of approximately ₹500 crore in FY27
ledger.quote: Based on the response provided in the chat, ₹500 crore appears to be a reasonable revenue guidance
ledger.actual: H1 FY27 reported consolidated revenue reached ₹241 crore (Q1: ₹117 crore, Q2: ₹124 crore).

ledger.promise: Achieve consolidated revenue of at least ₹700 crore in FY28
ledger.quote: consolidated revenue could be at least approximately ₹700 crore in FY2027–28.

credibility.label: low
credibility.summary: Management has repeatedly deferred and walked back core capital expenditure project completion dates across Project Jagruti, PM4, and the Guatemala unit. At the same time, debt expanded to ₹542 crore while operating performance dropped significantly in FY26 before showing a partial recovery in early FY27.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Management stated Project Jagruti funding delays were temporary and project was delayed, not derailed.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: FY26 PAT fell to ₹6 crore from ₹38 crore in FY25, while capital WIP built up to ₹597 crore and borrowings increased from ₹206 crore to ₹460 crore.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Management stated there is no doubt EBITDA margins should be 18% to 19% for FY27.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Reported EBITDA margins for Q1 FY27 were 13.1% and Q2 FY27 were 14.1%, averaging 13.3% across H1 FY27.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Management reported that borrowing costs increased from approximately 11% to 17%.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Consolidated borrowings grew from ₹184 crore in FY24 to ₹542 crore in FY27, driving up financing burden while Q2 FY27 PBT was ₹4 crore.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Management noted project postponement would allow internal accruals to come in.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: FY26 cash from operations was ₹75 crore against capital investing outflows of ₹367 crore, requiring total borrowings to rise to ₹460 crore.

bull.point: Sequential revenue momentum is recovering toward full-year targets.
bull.evidence: Quarterly revenue expanded from ₹101 crore in Q4 FY26 to ₹117 crore in Q1 FY27 and ₹124 crore in Q2 FY27, tracking toward the ₹500 crore FY27 target.

bull.point: Operating EBITDA margins have rebounded from FY26 lows.
bull.evidence: EBITDA margins improved from 2.3% in Q2 FY26 to 13.1% in Q1 FY27 and 14.1% in Q2 FY27.

bull.point: Project Jagruti financing is secured to enable near-term commissioning.
bull.evidence: Funding for Project Jagruti has been completed and machine commissioning is expected within a few months.

bear.point: Recurrent delays and pushbacks on key capital expansion projects.
bear.evidence: Project Jagruti target moved from CY2025 to end-FY26, August 2026, and Q3 FY27, while the Guatemala project was put in abeyance.

bear.point: Sharp increase in debt levels alongside elevated borrowing costs.
bear.evidence: Borrowings increased from ₹184 crore in FY24 to ₹542 crore in FY27 while interest rates rose from ~11% to ~17%.

bear.point: Current margin execution trails management guidance.
bear.evidence: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin averaged 13.3%, short of management's 18-19% guidance for FY27.
